by joann s . lublin

enron corp . may be the best - known name in the new economy , but for much of the past decade , the big energy trader was a little - known company with a smaller revenue base . enron expanded rapidly as a deregulated electricity market emerged in the late 1990 s , transforming the company from an electricity - trading boutique to a global conglomerate with a market capitalization of $ 61.5 billion at the close of regular trading thursday . since 1995 alone , enron ' s revenues have increased 33 % annually .  

" we are really the only place where electricity and natural gas are traded globally , " says michael l . miller , enron ' s chief financial officer . " if you want to trade in the new economy , you can ' t go anywhere else . "  

enron ' s revenues grew from $ 3.8 billion in 1995 to $ 19.6 billion in 2000 , according to the company . in the past 12 months , enron ' s revenues were $ 19.3 billion , a 33 % increase from the same period a year earlier , the company says .  

enron ' s rapid growth has been accompanied by a series of strategic moves that have helped it expand its reach into new markets . the company became a leading merchant of electricity and natural gas , owning power plants and pipelines . enron has also secured its position in the telecommunications and energy markets by buying stakes in power plants , pipelines and telecommunications firms around the world .  

enron ' s growth has been driven by three factors : deregulation of the telecommunications and energy industries , use of technology to manage complex trading deals and its trading expertise . the company ' s trading expertise comes from jeffrey r . skilling , the company ' s president , and andrew s . fastow , the firm ' s chief financial officer .  

" enron has grown by taking advantage of deregulation and the internet , " says richard schwartz , a securities analyst at thomson financial services . " anyone can use the internet to do business , but enron ' s success has been in getting all the pieces to work together . "  

when the telecommunications industry was deregulated in 1996 , the company bought a 25 % stake in idt corp . , a long - distance company . enron entered the broadband - cable field in 1999 with the purchase of providence starnet inc . , a broadband - cable company , for $ 5.75 billion . the purchase gave enron a foothold in the broadband - cable market with 1.8 million subscribers . enron plans to use the cable system to sell internet access and other services to homes and businesses .  

in the natural - gas industry , the company entered the business of building pipelines in 1998 with the purchase of pmi energy services for $ 4.2 billion . the purchase gave enron a stake in the business of building pipelines .  

" enron is a market - maker , " says richard j . seymour , a securities analyst at morgan stanley dean witter . " it operates in a number of different markets that are deregulating and is taking advantage of the deregulation . "  

enron has also developed a reputation for being an innovator . " one of the things that i really admire about enron is that they have been pioneers in the energy industry , " says richard carlson , chief executive of the gas utility division of american electric power . " they have been able to use technology well to improve their business . "  

enron also has a strong capital markets presence , says david a . morgan , chief executive of bear stearns & co . " they ' ve made a real effort to develop their capital markets business . "

minutes
dave convened a meeting today to assess the current status of the 2001 charter review . attendees included jeff , rick , mark , john , john , scott , and myself .

jeff provided an update on the 2001 charter review , which is on schedule but needs to be completed within the next 2 months . this review entails a thorough evaluation of each business unit to ascertain strategic fit and competitive advantages . the aim is to wrap this up by the 2nd quarter . objectives of the review are :

1 ) maintaining our competitive edge
2 ) ensuring alignment with the company ' s overarching strategy

jeff's plan involves each business unit submitting a business review addressing these points . these reviews will be examined by the respective management committee , who will then draft a high-level summary for jeff and the ceo ' s office . target for submission is friday , march 16th , with final reviews by friday , march 30th .

over the next 2 months , jeff will engage with each business unit to discuss these reviews . his overarching goal is to finalize the 2001 charter review by july 31st , 2001 .

agenda

2 ) expectations for each business unit in the review
3 ) responsibilities of each business unit regarding the review

discussion
jeff reiterated the status and timeline of the 2001 charter review , highlighting the immediate need for completion within the next 2 months . the review's purpose is to conduct a comprehensive evaluation of each business unit for strategic fit and competitive edge , with completion slated for the 2nd quarter . objectives include :

1 ) maintaining our competitive advantages
2 ) ensuring alignment with the company ' s strategy

jeff's directive is for each business unit to submit a detailed business review covering these elements . these will be vetted by the management committee for each unit , followed by a high-level overview for review by jeff and the ceo ' s office . the deadline for these reviews is friday , march 16th , with final versions due by friday , march 30th .

jeff intends to meet with each business unit over the next 2 months to discuss their business reviews , aiming to complete the entire 2001 charter review by july 31st , 2001 .

fcc ,

i spoke to you today regarding a conversation i had with mitchell lupin, a resident of chandler, ariz., and cousin of billie clark, recently elected to the fcc by president bush. mr. lupin recounted an encounter with a man who introduced himself as "ralph," claiming to be a friend of the president.

mr. lupin informed me that he was instructed by his cousin to reach out to the fcc about the spectrum auction's status and how it would be conducted. during the meeting, "ralph" requested mr. lupin's business card, upon which mr. lupin noted his affiliation with "chandler valley bank." "ralph" reciprocated with a card stating his name as tom m. alderson, a "strategic consultant" with "m.t.a. consulting."

mr. lupin expressed unease, mentioning that "ralph" inquired about his "position" at the fcc and requested contact details for his "senior staff." mr. lupin provided the secretary's office number but had no list of fcc staff on the auction committee. when asked about the auction's outcome, mr. lupin admitted he didn't know. he gave "ralph" his card, but has not heard from him since.

mr. lupin questioned "ralph's" claim of presidential friendship but noted his sincerity. he mentioned "ralph" was from texas but did not know his last name. mr. lupin, a republican himself, doubted any wrongdoing on "ralph's" part, as no confidential information was disclosed.

mr. lupin expressed deep concern about the encounter, wondering if he erred or if "ralph" was a republican plant seeking to discredit the fcc. he worried his cousin might be involved in disclosing information to the republican party.

i remain uncertain about the man's identity or intentions, whether he sought confidential information, or if mr. lupin unwittingly revealed anything sensitive. the possibility of "ralph" attempting to discredit the fcc or pass information to the republican party remains unknown. mr. lupin was genuinely troubled about his actions and the implications of the encounter.

fw : us financials and new england gas 

regis , 

this is a summary of my discussion about the new england gas business with dan and john . we believe that the business is in decline , primarily due to two factors : 1 ) the high fixed costs ( $ 1.0 - 1.9 / mmbtu ) and 2 ) the low variable costs ( ~$ 0.10 / mmbtu ) . 

there is a reason why the natural gas business is not a pure play on the price of natural gas . net margins remain almost constant , regardless of fluctuations in the price of natural gas . this is because the marginal cost of natural gas is very low . to generate profit , the price of natural gas must be raised above the marginal cost of production . 

the attached figure provides a breakdown of the fixed and variable costs . the fixed costs are amortized over a set volume of cubic feet . as the business volume declines , margins deteriorate because amortized ( fixed ) costs are distributed over fewer units . consequently , if all costs are eliminated , our profit from this business is minimal . 

the question remains : should we invest to restructure and reduce the fixed costs ? in my opinion , this business is not worth the investment . the marginal cost of natural gas is low , and the fixed costs are high . if further analysis is needed , i can provide a more detailed breakdown of the numbers . 

hopefully , this provides some clarity on the current state of the business . 

thanks ,

press release  
enron , cpc team up to form new energy company  
enron corporation and cpc international , inc . today announced a strategic alliance to form a new energy company , enron global energy corp . ( egc ) , to develop , finance , and operate energy projects worldwide . under the agreement , enron will transfer its energy assets to egc , which will be 60 percent owned by enron and 40 percent by cpc . enron will have a controlling 51 percent vote on the egc board of directors .  
enron and cpc will contribute their respective asset portfolios to egc , including a substantial lineup of power plants and oil and gas production and transportation assets globally . the new company anticipates generating approximately $ 1 billion in annual earnings and $ 100 million in annual cash flow , with the potential to nearly double these amounts once the assets are fully developed .  
enron ' s energy assets comprise 7 , 000 megawatts of power generation capacity , including four combined cycle gas turbines , which are among the most efficient and environmentally friendly power plants worldwide . enron ' s assets also include a 500 , 000 barrel per day oil pipeline , a 1 , 200 mile natural gas transmission system , and interests in global oil and gas projects . cpc ' s energy assets include a portfolio of power plants , including cogeneration facilities , as well as oil and gas production and transportation assets .  
enron ' s energy group has long been a market leader , developing one of the world ' s largest energy portfolios and successfully trading energy globally . enron ' s power generation assets have increased from 1 , 000 megawatts to over 7 , 000 megawatts since 1992 . by developing energy assets in emerging markets , enron has stimulated economic development while expanding its portfolio .  
egc will be a leading independent energy company worldwide and will possess one of the world ' s largest energy portfolios . the senior management team will include enron ' s current energy group management and senior management of cpc ' s energy division . the new company will be headquartered in houston , texas , with operations in the u . s . , the caribbean , the netherlands , india , singapore , hong kong , china , and australia . for more information , visit www . enroncorp . com .  
enron is a natural gas , electricity , communications , and paper company with global interests . enron is the world ' s largest wholesale trader of natural gas and electricity and the largest independent power producer in the u . s . enron ' s communications division , enron business communications services ( bcs ) , provides voice , data , and video services to over 500 , 000 business customers in 86 countries . enron is also a leading marketer of pulpwood and paper products . enron ' s common stock is traded on the new york stock exchange ( enr ) and the london stock exchange ( enrny ) .  
cpc international , inc . is a leading global supplier of energy , food , and fibers . cpc has expertise in the development , construction , acquisition , operation , and financing of energy , power , and related facilities , with extensive operations in the united states , europe , south america , the caribbean , asia , and the middle east .

the unemployment insurance program is a federal - state partnership that provides temporary income for workers who become unemployed through no fault of their own .  
benefits for up to 26 weeks for eligible claimants .  
in new mexico , the program is administered by the unemployment insurance division of the new mexico department of job and family services .  
qualify by working a minimum number of weeks and earning a minimum amount of wages during your base period .  
the base period is the first four of the last five completed calendar quarters preceding the date you file your claim .  
created by the social security act of 1935 , the national unemployment insurance program draws from the federal unemployment trust fund .  
funds also come from state unemployment insurance taxes paid by employers and interest earned on the trust fund .  
the federal government reimburses states for 90 percent of administrative costs and 50 percent of benefits costs .
